item.title: Silver selloff seems overdone, says Mirae Asset Sharekhan; here's why
item.description: The crude oil/silver ratio has fallen through the crucial support around 58, which means silver remains vulnerable to rise in oil prices.
item.dc:creator: Praveen Singh
item.content:encoded: Disclaimer: This article is written by Praveen Singh, head of commodities at Mirae Asset Sharekhan. Views expressed are his own. Readers' discretion is advised. Spot silver has been under tremendous pressure since it breached the crucial support around $58.60 on October 14. Numerous recovery attempts have been rebuffed around this level. The white metal fell more than $3 on October 22, losing 5.33 per cent to trade at $54.90, its lowest since July 17, as oil prices jumped.  Geopolitics and oilHighly volatile crude oil prices surged more than 3 per cent on October 22 on dwindling hopes of a US-Iran deal, as US President Trump denied talks with Iran. A drone attack on Aramco’s Shaybah field on October 21 killed two people, which amplified supply worries. Although crude oil flows through the Middle East have topped pre-war volumes, concerns over escalation of US-Iran tensions, steep crack spread, low SPR Reserves and lingering uncertainty over oil flows continue to support oil prices. Brent crude oil futures jumped to $112.68 on Thursday, the highest since May, and were up more than 3 per cent for the day.     ETFs and COMEX inventoryTotal known global silver ETF holdings rose to 805.76 Moz, the highest since March 25 as net inflows increased 5 Moz (65 Tons) since October 15. This is a healthy development for the metal as holdings had been hovering around 800 Moz in October, contrary to huge inflows into the gold ETFs. However, overall, ETFs currently hold 64 Moz (1991 tons) less silver, down 7.36 per cent YTD, as compared with the end of last year. ETFs have seen a net outflow of 26 Moz (809 tons) since the beginning of the Iran war. ALSO READ: Gold outlook bleak; avoid aggressive selling without stop loss: Analyst Registered COMEX silver inventory at 103.33 Moz is down ~49 per cent from the cycle peak of 201 Moz seen in September 2025. China’s silver inventoryShanghai Futures Exchange on warrant daily stock total stands at 1368 tons, down 8.25 per cent from the cycle peak of 1491 tons seen on September 30. However, silver stocks, as they surged sharply in the last seven months, are up 441 per cent from the cycle low of 252 tons reached on March 3.     One-month lease rateOne-month LBMA lease rate at 0 per cent shows ample float at the LBMA warehouses; hence, has bearish implications for the metal. India’s silver imports likely to riseIndia’s silver imports are expected to pickup after the government eased restrictions. Bloomberg reported traders and bank dealers have received quotas through permits covering up to 6000 tons of silver. These permits will be valid for six months. India had introduced new licensing requirements in May to restrict imports of the metal to cut down deficit. India imported 7000 tons of silver in 2025. As more metal gets imported into the country, silver premium has softened. US Dollar Index and yieldsThe US Dollar Index, which rose to 102.95 on October 14 in the wake of hotter-than-expected US CPI data for September, has been consolidating around in the 101.50-102 range. The Index, at the time of writing was hovering around 101.87, up 0.06 per cent for the day. US yields slid on Thursday. Two-year Treasury yieds were noted at 4.69 per cent, down 2.29 per cent for the day, and down 5.44 per cent from the cycle high of 4.94 per cent seen on October 14. 10-year yield was at 5.01 per cent, down over 2 per cent. October Fed rate hike probabilityTraders assign a probability of merely 7 per cent to the event of the Fed hiking rates at its October 28 meeting. OutlookCrude oil/silver ratio has fallen through the crucial support around 58, which means silver remains vulnerable to rise in oil prices. Although intrinsic fundamentals of the metal are not so encouraging, selloff in silver, as in case of gold, seems to be somewhat overdone as yields and dollar fell. Trend selling is weighing heavily on the metal. A decisive breach of support around $54.50 could take the metal to $48-$50 mark. Resistance is seen at $59.

item.title: Crude oil up 85% in 2026 poses threat to global economy; Brent may hit $120
item.description: Brent climbed back above $113 a barrel after a deadly drone strike on Saudi Aramco's Shaybah field, highlights Mohammed Imran of Mirae Asset Sharekhan.
item.dc:creator: Mohammed Imran
item.content:encoded: Disclaimer: Views and outlook in this report belong to the brokerages and analysts cited. They do not reflect the views of Business Standard. Readers are advised to exercise discretion. Mohammed Imran, research analyst, Mirae Asset Sharekhan Asian refining margines hit by higher Freights With no US-Iran deal in sight to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the rally in oil is ringing alarm bells across financial markets worldwide. Crude is up 85 per cent so far this year and 10 per cent in October alone, while spot Brent and Middle Eastern grades have held above $100 a barrel for two straight months, posing a threat to the global economy unlike any other. Brent climbed back above $113 a barrel after a deadly drone strike on Saudi Aramco's Shaybah field. Output there was not affected, but a separate attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed one person. US 10-year Treasury yield dropped 17 basis points in a single session to 4.96 per cent on 22 October, its first close below 5 per cent since 22 September, as a tech selloff drove investors into safe havens. Freight is eating Asian refiners Margins The crack spreads during July-September became a boon for Asian refiners which increased their throughput despite higher oil prices has they were able to offset with realization through exports to Europe and other geographies to benefit from the higher cracks margins, however the shortages of VLCC and other tankers has sent the shipping rates to sky high that has started to hurt the refinery margins  an Asian refinery running Middle East crude earned roughly $40 a barrel in gross margin, and about $36 of that went to the tanker. In January, the same Gulf-to-China voyage cost about $2 a barrel. March makes the contrast sharper: a $51 margin, $10 of freight, and $41 left for the refiner. The IEA uses about $36 a barrel, while a consultancy estimate published on 19 October puts freight at $33 and the refiner's share at $7. Which during July to September were around $20-25/b. China is already buying less. Its crude imports fell 21.5 per cent year on year in September as refiners drew down record stockpiles rather than pay up, and the industrial PMI breakdown shows inventories falling month after month. Q3 imports were down 29 per cent even though non-seaborne supply held flat. Russia's share rose to 27.4 per cent, and Sinopec now expects Chinese oil demand to fall 8.9 per cent this year. The IEA's October report notes that Asian margins on medium-sour crude turned negative in September. China's import cost rose just 33 per cent, to about 4,500 RMB/t, or roughly $87 a barrel. Even that figure is flattered: it includes the July ceasefire, when a lot of Iranian oil got out, and Q3 physical prices were well below recent levels. Gulf-to-China freight is normally far cheaper than shipping from the Americas, so Middle Eastern supply has clearly fallen sharply, and any claim that Gulf flows to China are near pre-war levels is hard to believe. Check - TOP GAINERS NSE | TOP LOSERS NSE  Indian refiners Delima The latest reports comes from the shipping’s trackers have shown increased shipments of Middle easter crude to Indian ports . Middle Eastern crude imports jumped to about 2.8 mb/d in September, the highest since February and back to pre-war levels, with Gulf oil making up about 54 per cent of total imports, up from 32 per cent in August. Russian imports fell about 14 per cent month on month to around 1.8 mb/d, cutting Russia's share to 33.5 per cent from 46.6 per cent as Indian refiners faced stiff competition from China. US crude, meanwhile, is losing ground in Asia. Leasing a tanker for the Pacific run now costs a record of almost $80 million, and Asian orders for November-delivery US crude have dropped roughly 50 per cent month on month to 24–26 million barrels. If that pace holds to the end of the month, it would be a seven-year low. US Weekly Crude Oil inventories This week's EIA data showed distillate stocks recovering from a record seasonal low, while gasoline inventories fell to their lowest level since 2014. Hurricane Isaias also cut US crude output by 0.4 mb/d. Gasoil and ULSD are both still near $200 a barrel. Globally, observed stocks edged down in September, as a 113 mb fall in onshore inventories more than offset a 103 mb surge in oil on water. That leaves global stocks 509 mb below pre-war levels. October 16 were US commercial crude oil stocks were -3.5 per cent below the seasonal 5-year average, gasoline inventories were -4.9 per cent below the seasonal 5-year average, and distillate inventories were -9.0 per cent below the 5-year seasonal average.  US crude oil production in the week ending October 16 fell sharply by -3.00 per cent w/w to 13.269 million bpd. What the Midterms Could Change With the US midterms set for 3 November, oil has turned into a political number. Gasoline is averaging $4.29 a gallon at US pumps and diesel $6.30, up more than $1.25 and nearly 75 per cent respectively from a year ago. Washington has leaned on temporary Russian diesel imports and a G7 release of 100 million barrels from emergency reserves, but we doubt these measures will bring prices down in the near term. In our view, an escalation would send Brent to test $120/b. A stalemate, by contrast, would keep WTI hovering around $100 and Brent anchored above $110, with refined products remaining tighter than crude. Any further strike on Saudi infrastructure would reopen the upside tail. So far, the global economy has absorbed the second-order effects of costlier crude, but at current prices, demand destruction is likely to set in over the coming months if the deadlock persists, although that is not our base case.

item.title: Gold outlook bleak; avoid aggressive selling without stop loss: Analyst
item.description: On October 22, spot gold prices fell through the support at $4066; thus, the metal moved out of its $4066-$4226 October range. The yellow metal broke below $4100 on surge in oil prices even as the ...
item.dc:creator: Praveen Singh
item.content:encoded: Disclaimer: This article is written by Praveen Singh, head of commodities at Mirae Asset Sharekhan. Views expressed are his own. Readers' discretion is advised. On October 22, spot gold prices fell through the support at $4066; thus, the metal moved out of its $4066-$4226 October range. The yellow metal broke below $4100 on surge in oil prices even as the dollar index and yields were largely subdued. Firming up of the dollar as the day wore on pulled down the metal further. As of Thursday night, spot gold was trading at $4037, the lowest since August 3. It was down 2.5 per cent for the day. Geopolitics and oilCrude oil prices surged more than 3 per cent on October 22 on dwindling hope of the US-Iran deal as the US President Trump denied Iran talks. A drone attack on Aramco’s Shaybah field on October 21 killed two people, which amplified supply worries. Although crude oil flows through the Middle East have topped pre-war volumes, concerns over escalation of US-Iran tensions, steep crack spread, low SPR Reserves and lingering uncertainty over oil flows continue to support oil prices. Brent crude oil futures jumped to $112.68 on Thursday, highest since May, and were up more than 3 per cent for the day.  ALSO READ: Crude oil up 85% in 2026 poses threat to global economy; Brent may hit $120   Gold ETFGold ETF flows remain quite encouraging. Total net global gold ETF holdings rose to 101.55 Moz, highest since July 2022, as ETFs recorded a net inflow of 0.68 Moz in October. ETFs’ holdings are now up 2.60 Moz (81 tons) YTD and up 0.63 Moz (20 tons) since the beginning of the Iran war on February 28. Data roundupThis week is light on the US data front. ADP weekly employment change data for the week ending October 3 came in at 18.5K as compared to 26K in the previous week. US housing data were disappointing. NAHB Housing Index fell from 32 in September to 29 in October -- lowest since 2012. Housing starts in September slumped from 1288K in August to 1221K (forecast 1305K), a six-year low excluding the May data. Similarly, pending home sales fell 7.3 per cent on the month in September versus the estimate of -0.5 per cent. Jobless claims rose from 7K to 303.K. Weekly jobless claims slid from 200K to 194K, while continuing claims rose from 1703K to 1728K. Overall, weekly job data remain healthy in ‘low hire, low fire’ scenario.  September Leading Index was steady against the forecast of -0.1 per cent. UK's employment report for September was mixed. Average weekly earnings slowed down from August. Earnings rose 3.7 per cent Y-o-Y versus the estimate of 3.8 per cent and prior 3.9 per cent. 3M-3M employment change at 102K topped the estimate of 5K, while 3 months unemployment rate edged lower from 4.9 per cent to 4.7 per cent (forecast 4.9 per cent). UK’s September CPI inflation were hotter-than-expected. CPI inflation rose 3.5 per cent Y-o-Y compared with the estimate of 3.4 per cent and 3.1 per cent prior, while it was up 0.4 per cent M-o-M versus the forecast of 0.3 per cent. The headline CPI reading is the hottest since October 2025. Core CPI rose 2.8 per cent Y-o-Y, in line with the forecast but hotter than the August reading of 2.6 per cent.  ALSO READ: Silver ETFs fall up to 5% as oil surge, inflation fears hit bullion markets US Dollar Index and yieldsThe US Dollar Index, which rose to 102.95 on October 14 in the wake of hotter-than-expected US CPI data for September, has been consolidating around in the 101.50-102 range. The index, at the time of writing was hovering around 101.87, up 0.06 per cent for the day. US yields slid on Thursday. Two-year yields were noted at 4.69 per cent, down 2.29 per cent for the day, and down 5.44 per cent from the cycle high of 4.94 per cent seen on October 14; 10-year yield was at 5.01 per cent, down over 2 per cent. October Fed rate hike probabilityTraders assign a probability of merely 7 per cent to the event of the Fed hiking rates at its October 28 meeting. World Gold Council’s researchAccording to Kavita Chacko, research head for India at the World Gold Council (WGC), domestic gold price discounts for gold narrowed sharply in October. Discounts dropped from an average of $66 per ounce in September to $8 as of October 16 on improving seasonal demand. Seasonal gold demand is gaining strength in annual festive and wedding period as recent decline in gold prices supports demand. Gold bar and coin demand has moderated this year on waning price momentum. Net ETF inflows rose to US $466.2 million in September, the highest in seven months and nearly 3 tons of gold were added to holdings during the month, taking the cumulative holdings to 124 tons. Central bank watchChina’s PBoC kept one-year and five-year Loan Prime Rates unchanged at 3 per cent and 3.5 per cent in its policy announced on October 20. The US federal Reserve will deliver its monetary policy on October 28. The European Central Bank will announce its monetary policy on October 29. It is widely expected that both the central banks will keep their respective rates unchanged. However, major focus will be on the Fed’s stance on future monetary policy meetings as investors gear up for a rate hike in December FOMC meeting, though the Fed Chair Warsh adhering to his policy of ‘no forward guidance’ will abstain from giving any clear signals.  UK Chancellor of the exchequer John Healey will present annual budget to the Parliament on October 28. The Office for Budget Responsibility will release its fiscal and economic forecasts the same day. Upcoming dataMajor US data on card in the near term include ADP weekly employment change (October 27), October Conference Board Consumer Confidence (October 27), September preliminary durable goods orders (October 27), new home sales (October 27), September Advance goods trade balance (October 28), September real personal spending (October 29), Q3 GDP and September PCE Price Index (October 29). Major Eurozone data include S&P Global Eurozone manufacturing, services and composite PMIs (October 23). UK's PMIs will also be released on October 23. Japan's September national CPI and October preliminary PMI data will be released on October 23.   ALSO READ: Silver slips below ₹2 lakh amid selling pressure; gold also declinesOutlookSharp decline in gold prices on October 22 came mainly on higher oil prices, which looks somewhat overdone as the US yields fell. In addition, weak US housing data and mounting fiscal and political worries in France and social protests in several European countries provide a supportive backdrop for the meta. It appears selloff intensified on momentum selling. Near-term resistance is at $4140/$4227; support is at $4000/$3930. As oil prices are expected to rise further, the shiny metal may fall further, though selling aggressively at the prevailing levels without a strict stoploss should be avoided. A decisive breach of $4000 support will bring the key support at $3930 in focus.

item.title: Apple's iPhone Duo hits stores in face of short supply, high demand
item.description: The iPhone lineup is Apple’s largest moneymaker, generating roughly half of the company’s revenue. And the Duo is the biggest single design change in the device’s nearly two-decade history. Though the ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Mark Gurman Apple Inc. has already shown there’s a strong appetite for its $2,000-and-up foldable iPhone Duo. Now it needs to meet that demand. The new device goes on sale Friday, with the first shipments reaching Apple retail stores around the world. It also will begin arriving at the homes of customers who ordered quickly enough to secure day-one deliveries. The launch is bringing back a once-familiar sight: lines outside Apple stores. Such crowds have largely disappeared in recent years after Apple, retailers like Best Buy Co. and wireless carriers began maintaining enough inventory to fulfill most orders through home delivery or appointment-based store pickups. This time is different. Supplies for preorders were so limited that many customers hoping to get the Duo on launch day have little choice but to line up and see whether their local store has any inventory available. Apple is allocating a small portion of its stock for those people.  At the company’s flagship Fifth Avenue store in New York City, where top Apple executives typically open the doors to buyers, there was a line of customers without preorders that reached more than a few dozen people by the early evening on Thursday. There were similar lines in Asia and Australia. As one of the most expensive mainstream smartphones ever sold, the Duo had raised questions about just how much demand there would be. But early adopters, resellers and everyday Apple fans have demonstrated that the interest is there. The iPhone lineup is Apple’s largest moneymaker, generating roughly half of the company’s revenue. And the Duo is the biggest single design change in the device’s nearly two-decade history. Though the company wasn’t first to market with a foldable phone, it looks to gain an edge with a more polished product built for Apple fans. Rather than a repeat of the lackluster debut of the Vision Pro headset nearly three years ago, the Duo’s launch is shaping up to be a throwback to the iPhone introductions of old — when demand far outstripped supply. That’s the case even with device prices reaching as high as $3,199 for models with 2 terabytes of storage. Though the Duo’s cost sets a record for a mass-market smartphone, Apple’s competitors such as Samsung Electronics Co. have been raising prices as well. Shortages of memory chips and other components have made consumer electronics more expensive across the board.  Consumers placing new orders for the Duo on Apple’s website are now being offered delivery at the end of January, though some early buyers have seen their January shipping estimates move up to as soon as November or December. The delays mark some of the lengthiest for a new Apple product in the company’s modern era. The phones are difficult to produce because of their advanced hinge and new display technology. They’re also only built in a limited number of facilities in China. Apple expanded production in recent years for its traditional iPhones, including to India, which has helped with supply.  Apple reports its quarterly earnings results on Nov. 2, but the period won’t include sales of the Duo because the period concluded around the end of September. It will reflect early sales of iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models, which debuted on Sept. 18. Other new versions, such as the entry-level iPhone or the updated Air, won’t go on sale until next year, Bloomberg News has reported. That marks a change in the company’s usual release schedule, a move meant to help spread out revenue across the year.
